For this reason, recent efforts have been made to employ advanced LLMs, such as GPT series ( OpenAI, 2023 ; OpenAI, 2024 ; OpenAI, 2025 ) , Gemini series ( Google, 2023 ; Google, 2024 ; Google, 2025 ) , and Claude series ( Anthropic, 2024a ; Anthropic, 2024b ; Anthropic, 2025 ) , to generate synthetic data for LLM fine-tuning ( Josifoski et al., 2023 ; Gupta et al., 2023 ; Long et al., 2024 ; Qin et al., 2025 ) . It has been shown that in most domains, advanced expert LLMs are capable of generating high-quality data that can benefit others ( Ubani et al., 2023 ; Peng et al., 2023 ; Xu et al., 2023 ; Yang et al., 2024 ; Choi et al., 2024 ; Zhang, 2024 ; Wang et al., 2024b ; DeepSeek-AI et al., 2025 ) . Compared to these studies, our self-play fine-tuning method focuses on using data generated by the current policy model to train itself to achieve the progressive performance improvements, and offers an alternative to expert-LLM-based strategies. 
 6 Conclusion and discussion 
 In this paper, we investigate self-play fine-tuning for LLMs and identify two issues of the existing method 𝚂𝙿𝙸𝙽 \mathtt{SPIN} : unstable optimization during iterations and misalignment between training and generation. To address these issues, we propose a novel self-play fine-tuning method named 𝚃 ​ - ​ 𝚂𝙿𝙸𝙽 \mathtt{T}\mbox{-}\mathtt{SPIN} with two key designs. First, our 𝚃 ​ - ​ 𝚂𝙿𝙸𝙽 \mathtt{T}\mbox{-}\mathtt{SPIN} simultaneously optimizes the current advantage of the annotated response 𝐲 \mathbf{y} over the newly generated response 𝐲 ′ \mathbf{y}^{\prime} , and the historical advantage of 𝐲 ′ \mathbf{y}^{\prime} over the proto-synthetic response 𝐲 0 \mathbf{y}_{0} . When current advantages vanish, historical advantages can still guide the fine-tuning process, avoiding the unstable optimization. Second, 𝚃 ​ - ​ 𝚂𝙿𝙸𝙽 \mathtt{T}\mbox{-}\mathtt{SPIN} incorporates the entropy constraint into the self-play framework, which eliminates the need for a reference policy in the reward computations, thus aligning the reward formulation and the generation metric. Empirically, we conduct extensive experiments and examine the performances of 𝚃 ​ - ​ 𝚂𝙿𝙸𝙽 \mathtt{T}\mbox{-}\mathtt{SPIN} on a variety of tasks. Experimental results show that 𝚃 ​ - ​ 𝚂𝙿𝙸𝙽 \mathtt{T}\mbox{-}\mathtt{SPIN} maintains stable evolution and achieves better performance than its contenders, and outperforms supervised fine-tuning by leveraging only 25 % 25\% annotated data. 
 Limitations and future work. 
There are several promising directions for future research. First, at each iteration, 𝚃 ​ - ​ 𝚂𝙿𝙸𝙽 \mathtt{T}\mbox{-}\mathtt{SPIN} needs to re-generate synthetic responses for all prompts, although some of them may no longer contribute to further evolutions. Consequently, a carefully designed filter strategy is necessary to choose valuable samples before generation. Second, in 𝚃 ​ - ​ 𝚂𝙿𝙸𝙽 \mathtt{T}\mbox{-}\mathtt{SPIN} , the expert-annotated data is fixed during iterations. But, in real-world applications, the target distribution may shift over time, and hence the fixed annotated samples may not be suitable for online fine-tuning. For this reason, self-play fine-tuning for non-stationary target distributions is another interesting direction, for which we believe that some advanced techniques from online learning may offer valuable insights ( Hazan, 2016 ; Orabona, 2019 ; Zhang et al., 2018 ; Wang et al., 2024c ; Wang et al., 2024e ) .
